issues.legal_issue: A land-acquisition notification is invalid when public notice of its substance in the locality is not given alongside or immediately after its official publication.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was published in the official gazette.
Public notice of the substance of the notification was not given in the locality until substantially later.
The affected landowner filed objections after the period for objections had expired.
issues.conclusion: The notification did not comply with the mandatory requirements and was invalid. The High Court was justified in quashing the acquisition proceedings, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 requires both publication of the notification in the Official Gazette and public notice of its substance at convenient places in the locality; the local notice must accompany or immediately follow the gazette publication. This local notice is mandatory because, without it, interested persons may be deprived of the valuable right to object under section 5A(1), which allows objections within thirty days after issue of the notification. The Court agreed with Gangadharaiah v. State of Mysore and Ors. (1961 Mys. L.J. 883).

predicates.land_acquisition_notification_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a notification issued for a land acquisition.
predicates.official_publication: The acquisition notification was published in the official gazette.
predicates.locality_notice_accompanied_or_immediate: Public notice of the substance of the notification was given in the locality at the same time as, or immediately after, official publication.

issues.definition: When a challenged land-acquisition notification was officially published but local notice did not accompany or immediately follow that publication, the notification is invalid.
